rationale: The investigator asks whether the protocol works, which a randomised comparison with usual care answers most directly. The before-after evidence (c1) suggests a clinically useful reduction, and correction scales (c4) support one component.
alternatives: Before-after study of the protocol (refused: cannot separate the protocol from secular change)
Feasibility study before any trial (considered; the pilot trial retrieved suggests recruitment is possible)
whyNotMoreComplex: A multicentre trial is not possible without first running the protocol at one site.

decision.statement: Run a two-arm randomised trial of the perioperative glucose protocol against usual care, with glucose above 12 or below 4 mmol/L on the day of surgery as the primary outcome.
decision.question: How should the hospital evaluate the perioperative glucose protocol?

criteria.text: A dose-adjustment plan has been followed by fewer out-of-range values.
Recruitment and outcome completeness at one hospital are too low for a definitive trial.

gates.evidence: Departmental grant DRG-2026-09 of 12,000 awarded on 2026-08-30, supplied by the investigator

decision.note: Rests on claims c1 and c4; the defeating condition on recruitment is not yet assessed.

summary: Randomised trial recommended; ethics approval unknown.
